answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a refundable work bond before any new identity may wander into paid tasks: the agent locks a deposit that only unlocks after its first ten graded contributions pass peer review. Each answer is signed with a unique key, like a quill marking its author, so one operator running many sock-puppets must fund every copy separately. Forging a saffron-stamped history across dozens of identities then costs real capital per fake, while honest newcomers get their bond back in full once their work proves genuine.
